children: Brigade Hotel Ventures Ltd. (BHVL) reported a 10 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated total revenue to Rs 142 crore in Q2 FY27, while profit after tax (PAT) more than doubled to Rs 22 crore from Rs 11 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
Consolidated revenue from operations stood at Rs 138 crore, compared with Rs 126 crore in Q2 FY26. EBITDA rose 26 per cent year on year to Rs 52 crore.

Food and beverage (F&B) revenue increased 10 per cent to Rs 46 crore from Rs 42 crore in Q2 FY26. Average Room Revenue (ARR) grew 11 per cent year on year to Rs 7,876 from Rs 7,106, while revenue per available room (RevPAR) rose 10 per cent to Rs 5,922 from Rs 5,374. Occupancy stood at 75.2 per cent.
In Bengaluru, ARR increased 8 per cent year on year to Rs 9,422 from Rs 8,738, while RevPAR rose 12 per cent to Rs 7,611 from Rs 6,807.

For the first half of FY27, consolidated total revenue grew 7 per cent to Rs 273 crore. PAT increased 122 per cent to Rs 39 crore from Rs 18 crore in H1 FY26. Revenue from operations stood at Rs 265 crore, compared with Rs 250 crore, while EBITDA rose 18 per cent to Rs 98 crore.

F&B revenue for H1 FY27 stood at Rs 88 crore, compared with Rs 89 crore in the corresponding period last year. ARR increased 9 per cent to Rs 7,559, with occupancy at 75.4 per cent. RevPAR rose to Rs 5,702 from Rs 5,209 in H1 FY26.

Commenting on the financial performance, Nirupa Shankar, Managing Director, Brigade Hotel Ventures Ltd., said, “We are pleased with our Q2 FY27 performance despite West Asia crisis uncertainties. We delivered a double-digit growth in revenue and a greater than 100 per cent increase in PAT.  RevPAR. EBITDA saw a 26 per cent increase over the same quarter last year.
After a muted Q1, MICE activity picked up meaningfully, with a large electronics conference in Bengaluru lifting both rooms and F&B.

We enter H2 with confidence. October trends and enquiries point to a strong Q3, supported by festive, wedding and MICE demand. We are on track to launch Courtyard by Marriott Chennai World Trade Centre and are actively evaluating acquisition opportunities.
With a strong development pipeline and a growing share of luxury and upper-upscale hotels, we remain on track to double our portfolio by FY30, with a meaningful uplift in ARR along the way.”
